table.name: HPFP Solenoid End Offset
table.description: Crank angle subtracted from the pump command to give the end of the solenoid's energised window, by rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Solenoid Window Start
table.description: Start of the pump solenoid's energised window, by battery voltage and rpm, as a crank angle in the pump frame. Used whenever the engine is running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure Additive Multiplier
table.description: Scaling (255 = x1.0) for Target Rail Pressure Additive, by an unidentified input and what is probably intake air temperature. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Integral Step
table.description: How much the rail-pressure controller's integral term moves each 10 ms pass, toward removing a steady pressure error. Higher = faster correction, more risk of hunting. This set is used only while bit 0 of the switch byte that also holds Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is set (value 1). While that bit is clear, the rail-pressure controller runs on the (Set 2) tables. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Integral Step (Set 2)
table.description: How much the rail-pressure controller's integral term moves each 10 ms pass, toward removing a steady pressure error. Higher = faster correction, more risk of hunting. The controller that reads the unnumbered set runs only while bit 0 of the switch byte that also holds Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is set (value 1). With bit 0 or bit 1 of that byte set, the Set 2 controller still runs but limits its result differently. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Solenoid Window End Limit
table.description: Upper limit on the end of the pump solenoid's energised window, by battery voltage and rpm, as a crank angle. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Solenoid Window End Limit (Alternate)
table.description: Upper limit on the end of the pump solenoid's energised window, by battery voltage and rpm, as a crank angle. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Proportional Gain
table.description: Proportional gain of the rail-pressure controller, by rpm: how hard the pump command reacts to pressure error. Higher = faster but risks oscillation. This set is used only while bit 0 of the switch byte that also holds Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is set (value 1). While that bit is clear, the rail-pressure controller runs on the (Set 2) tables. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Proportional Gain (Set 2)
table.description: Proportional gain of the rail-pressure controller, by rpm: how hard the pump command reacts to pressure error. Higher = faster but risks oscillation. The controller that reads the unnumbered set runs only while bit 0 of the switch byte that also holds Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is set (value 1). With bit 0 or bit 1 of that byte set, the Set 2 controller still runs but limits its result differently. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0)
table.description: Rail pressure target during cranking (combustion mode 0), by coolant and rpm. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure Additive
table.description: Extra rail pressure added to Target Rail Pressure, scaled by Target Rail Pressure Additive Multiplier, only with no rail-pressure sensor faults. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (8-bit)
table.description: 8-bit copy of the target rail pressure map (engine speed x load) that feeds a second fuel-pressure output; its values times 150 equal the main map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure Additive (8-bit)
table.description: Additive for the 8-bit target rail pressure path, scaled by Target Rail Pressure Additive Multiplier. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Scaling
table.description: Injector size constant, shown as the injector flow (g/s) the ECU assumes at the 0.3 MPa reference of Injector Flow Compensation. Cranking pulses, latency, minimum pulse and the throttle-rate transient fuel are in microseconds and do not follow it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Maximum
table.description: Upper limit applied to the base fuel quantity. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Command Minimum
table.description: Lower limit of the high-pressure pump command, a crank angle in the pump frame. The upper limit is HPFP Command Maximum Base plus HPFP Command Range, so raising this does not raise the upper limit; keep it below that. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Command Maximum Base
table.description: Base of the high-pressure pump command upper limit: the limit is this + HPFP Command Range. Raise this (or the Range) to raise the upper limit; HPFP Command Minimum does not move it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: HPFP Command Range
table.description: Range of the high-pressure pump command: the upper limit is HPFP Command Maximum Base + this, so it does not move with HPFP Command Minimum. Also used by the pump solenoid circuit monitor. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description: Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop fuel target (AFR) by engine speed and load, for TGVs closed with AVCS inactive. The ECU blends the four main maps rather than switching between them: TGV Closed against TGV Open by how far the TGVs are open, and AVCS Inactive against AVCS Active by a weight that ramps toward Active while both cams are in their normal control states. The same weight blends the Primary Ignition (TGV …, AVCS …) maps. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop fuel target (AFR) by engine speed and load, for TGVs open with AVCS inactive. The ECU blends the four main maps rather than switching between them: TGV Closed against TGV Open by how far the TGVs are open, and AVCS Inactive against AVCS Active by a weight that ramps toward Active while both cams are in their normal control states. The same weight blends the Primary Ignition (TGV …, AVCS …) maps. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop fuel target (AFR) by engine speed and load, for TGVs closed with AVCS active. The ECU blends the four main maps rather than switching between them: TGV Closed against TGV Open by how far the TGVs are open, and AVCS Inactive against AVCS Active by a weight that ramps toward Active while both cams are in their normal control states. The same weight blends the Primary Ignition (TGV …, AVCS …) maps. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop fuel target (AFR) by engine speed and load, for TGVs open with AVCS active. The ECU blends the four main maps rather than switching between them: TGV Closed against TGV Open by how far the TGVs are open, and AVCS Inactive against AVCS Active by a weight that ramps toward Active while both cams are in their normal control states. The same weight blends the Primary Ignition (TGV …, AVCS …) maps. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Open Loop Enrichment B
table.description: Second open-loop enrichment map; the larger of the open-loop terms is used. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Open Loop Delay Load Threshold
table.description: Load, by rpm, above which the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group takes effect after a delay; below it that group is off. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive by DAM (128 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Knock-dependent extra enrichment for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its DAM multiplier (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed Loop Fueling Target
table.description: Closed-loop fuelling target by engine speed and load (128 = stoichiometric). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Idle, Positive Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal released and positive error. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Cold, Positive Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant below 50 degC and positive error. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Warm, Positive Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant at or above 50 degC and positive error. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Idle, Negative Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal released and negative error. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Cold, Negative Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant below 50 degC and negative error. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Warm, Negative Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant at or above 50 degC and negative error. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Closed Loop Learning Step
table.description: How much long-term fuel trim changes per learning update, by the size of the averaged closed-loop correction. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Stoichiometric AFR
table.description: Stoichiometric air/fuel ratio used by the fuel model (14.7). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed Loop Minimum Target
table.description: Richest target allowed in closed loop: if the target is richer than this, the ECU switches to open loop. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Scales the TGV transition fuel adders by coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Extra Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Part of an extra fuel pulse on fast tip-in. Scales the extra pulse by coolant (64 = x1.0), out of neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Extra Pulse Coolant Multiplier (Neutral)
table.description: Part of an extra fuel pulse on fast tip-in. Scales the extra pulse by coolant (64 = x1.0) while in neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 0)
table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 1)
table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 2)
table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 3)
table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment (Closing)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to move, below 3600 rpm and only when cold (TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier). Initial amount after a closing event, by rpm and load. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment (Closing, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of TGV Transition Enrichment (Closing), used under an unidentified condition. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Film Gain (Coolant)
table.description: Scales the transient film step by coolant temperature (64 = 1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Film Gain (Coolant, AT/CVT)
table.description: As Transient Fuel Film Gain (Coolant), on AT/CVT codings. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Film Gain (Coolant, MT Coding)
table.description: As Transient Fuel Film Gain (Coolant), on the manual coding when the alternate selection applies. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Extra Pulse RPM Multiplier
table.description: Part of an extra fuel pulse on fast tip-in. Scales the extra pulse by rpm (128 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales the throttle-movement transient fuel by rpm (256 = x1.0). Raise it for more tip-in fuel at that rpm. Not active for the first second with the pedal released or at steady idle at standstill. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Term Minimum
table.description: Largest fuel reduction the throttle-closing side of the transient fuel may command, by coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Film Gain RPM Multiplier (Negative Film)
table.description: Scales the film term by engine speed while the film term is negative (fuel taken away). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Film Gain RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales the load-rise (film) transient fuel by rpm while it adds fuel (128 = x1.0). Companion of Transient Fuel Film Target. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Hold Time (Closing)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to move, below 3600 rpm and only when cold (TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier). How long the closing adder is held before fading. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Hold Time (Opening)
table.description: How long the TGV-opening fuel adder is held before fading. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Closing)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to move, below 3600 rpm and only when cold (TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier). How fast the closing adder fades after its hold, by rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Opening)
table.description: How fast the TGV-opening fuel adder fades after its hold. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Closing, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Closing), used under an unidentified condition. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Opening, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Opening), used under an unidentified condition. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain
table.description: Acceleration/deceleration fuel on throttle movement, by coolant: larger = more fuel when the throttle opens and less when it closes. The table the manual car uses, every pass while running. Keep the three Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain tables consistent. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain (Alternate B)
table.description: Version B of Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain, selected by status flags. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain (Alternate A)
table.description: Version A of Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain, selected by status flags. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: How fast the cranking fuel floor fades after the engine starts, by start coolant, on a repeat attempt. 65536 = no decay, smaller = faster fade. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel for a stall-window restart, repeat attempt. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the secondary cranking fuel by coolant when rail pressure is still low some time into a start (64 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Decay (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: How fast the secondary cranking fuel floor fades after the engine starts, by start coolant, on a repeat attempt (per 10 ms pass). 65536 = no decay, smaller = faster fade. Keep equal to Cranking Fuel Decay (Repeat Attempt). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Decay (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Post-start fade of the secondary cranking fuel for a stall-window restart, repeat attempt. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Pedal Multiplier
table.description: Cranking fuel multiplier by accelerator position. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales the largest of the three after-start enrichments by rpm (128 = x1.0) while cranking and running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Low Rail Pressure Start Enrichment
table.description: Extra fuel by coolant when rail pressure is still low some time into a start, until pressure has stayed close to target for a while. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start History Reset Delay (Coolant)
table.description: Time after ignition-off, by coolant, after which the ECU forgets the previous start, so the next start counts as a first start rather than a restart. Shorter with a weak battery. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (Special Start, TGV Closed)
table.description: Special-start version of the cranking fuel rpm multiplier, TGV Closed side (255 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (Special Start, TGV Open)
table.description: Special-start version of the cranking fuel rpm multiplier, TGV Open side (255 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay (First Attempt)
table.description: How fast the cranking fuel floor fades away after the engine starts, by start coolant, on a first attempt. 65536 = no decay, smaller = faster fade. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay (Stall Window, First Attempt)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel for a stall-window restart, first attempt. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Restart after Key-Off)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant, chosen by start type. Start type: restart after key-off. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Restart after Stall)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant, chosen by start type. Start type: restart after stall. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Special Start, Alternate)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant for start type: Special Start, Alternate (65536 = no decay). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Special Start, Initial, Alternate)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant for start type: Special Start, Initial, Alternate (65536 = no decay). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant, chosen by start type. Stall-window restart, start type: special start. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start, Initial)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant, chosen by start type. Stall-window restart, start type: special start, initial. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start, Initial, Alternate)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant for start type: Stall Window, Special Start, Initial, Alternate (65536 = no decay). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary RPM Multiplier (Special Start, TGV Closed)
table.description: Special-start version of the cranking fuel rpm multiplier, TGV Closed side (255 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary RPM Multiplier (Special Start, TGV Open)
table.description: Special-start version of the cranking fuel rpm multiplier, TGV Open side (255 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Repeat Attempt, Special Start)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse for a repeat attempt in the special start type. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt, Special Start)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse for a stall-window restart, repeat attempt, special start type. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start)
table.description: Secondary-path copy of Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start, Initial)
table.description: Secondary-path copy of Cranking Fuel Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start, Initial). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Decay by Start Type (Stall Window, Special Start, Initial, Alternate)
table.description: Post-start fade of cranking fuel by start coolant for start type: Stall Window, Special Start, Initial, Alternate (65536 = no decay). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Barometric Multiplier
table.description: Cranking fuel multiplier by what is probably barometric pressure, for starting at altitude. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (First Attempt)
table.description: Main cranking fuel pulse by coolant, for a normal first cranking attempt. Raise for more fuel while cranking. Raw units: change it proportionally. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant used on a repeat attempt, after a previous attempt already injected fuel and reached 800 rpm or cranked a while. Raw units: change it proportionally. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Repeat Attempt, Special Start)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a repeat attempt in the special start type. Raw units: the factors' normalisation is not fully resolved, so change it proportionally. Confidence: inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Repeat Attempt, Special Start, Alternate)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a repeat special-start attempt when the extra start condition is not met (the other special-start table carries the normal values). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Stall Window, First Attempt)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a restart after a stop inside a calibrated coolant window, first attempt. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a stall-window restart, repeat attempt. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt, Special Start)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a stall-window restart, repeat attempt, special start type. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt, Special Start, Alternate)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a repeat special-start attempt when the extra start condition is not met (the other special-start table carries the normal values). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (First Attempt)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse by coolant (first attempt). It is the cranking pulse whenever the engine cranks in normal combustion mode instead of the start mode: after about 10 s of continuous cranking, when the low-rail-pressure start latch is set (then scaled by Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier), or on a re-crank before the start sequence reset; it also sets a floor on fuel in normal running until it decays. Raw units: change it proportionally. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse by coolant (repeat attempt). It is the cranking pulse whenever the engine cranks in normal combustion mode instead of the start mode: after about 10 s of continuous cranking, when the low-rail-pressure start latch is set (then scaled by Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier), or on a re-crank before the start sequence reset; it also sets a floor on fuel in normal running until it decays. Raw units: change it proportionally. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Repeat Attempt, Special Start, Alternate)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a repeat special-start attempt when the extra start condition is not met (the other special-start table carries the normal values). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Stall Window, First Attempt)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse for a stall-window restart, first attempt. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse for a stall-window restart, repeat attempt. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt, Special Start, Alternate)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a repeat special-start attempt when the extra start condition is not met (the other special-start table carries the normal values). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Key-Off)
table.description: Multiplier on the cranking fuel by coolant when restarting after the engine was switched off with the key (start type meaning inferred). Edit with Cranking Fuel Secondary Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Key-Off). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Stall)
table.description: Multiplier on the cranking fuel by coolant when restarting after a stall with the ignition still on (start type meaning inferred). Edit with the Secondary copy. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Special Start)
table.description: Cranking fuel multiplier by coolant for the special start type (255 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Special Start, Alternate)
table.description: Cranking fuel multiplier by coolant for the special start type, Alternate (255 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injection Timing (TGV Open)
table.description: Direct-injection timing (start of injection) for the single-injection running mode, by engine speed and load, used while the accelerator is pressed. Degrees before compression TDC: larger = earlier. Values around 280-360 BTDC are on the intake stroke (360 = the TDC between exhaust and intake). The ECU blends the TGV-open and TGV-closed maps by TGV opening, then applies the matching Injection Timing Correction scaled by its weight. The units follow the FA24 injection-angle code (720 - raw/2), which this ECU's scheduler splits the same way; not yet confirmed on a car. Change in small steps and log knock and fuel trims: injection timing affects mixture preparation, smoke and plug fouling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injection Timing (TGV Closed)
table.description: Direct-injection timing (start of injection) for the single-injection running mode, by engine speed and load, used while the accelerator is pressed. Degrees before compression TDC: larger = earlier. Values around 280-360 BTDC are on the intake stroke (360 = the TDC between exhaust and intake). The ECU blends the TGV-open and TGV-closed maps by TGV opening, then applies the matching Injection Timing Correction scaled by its weight. The units follow the FA24 injection-angle code (720 - raw/2), which this ECU's scheduler splits the same way; not yet confirmed on a car. Change in small steps and log knock and fuel trims: injection timing affects mixture preparation, smoke and plug fouling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Spark Retard
table.description: How far spark is retarded from base timing during cold-start catalyst heating (combustion mode 2), by the requested spark torque share: the less of the torque the spark is asked to deliver, the more retard, which heats the catalyst faster. The spark moves toward this target in steps. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Exit Threshold (Neutral Switch Off)

table.name: Catalyst Heating Readiness Idle Stability Time
table.description: How long the idle must be steady (pedal released, normal running) before the catalyst-heating readiness flag sets, by rpm change and rpm versus idle target. Its exact role after that is inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Bypass Flags
table.description: Start-sequence switches. Bit 7 (add 128) skips the whole cold-start combustion sequence and holds the combustion mode at Start Sequence Bypass Combustion Mode from key-on, including cranking. Not recommended: Catalyst Heating Coolant Maximum/Minimum are the cleaner way to drop the warm-up phases. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Bypass Combustion Mode
table.description: Combustion mode held while bit 7 of Start Sequence Bypass Flags is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Coolant Maximum
table.description: The cold-start sequence (warm-up combustion modes) runs only when coolant is at or below this at the end of cranking; above it the engine goes straight to normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Coolant Minimum
table.description: The cold-start sequence runs only when coolant is at or above this; below it the engine goes straight to normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Minimum RPM
table.description: Engine speed the engine must reach after cranking for the cold-start sequence to start; otherwise it goes straight to normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Start Coolant Maximum
table.description: The cold-start sequence runs only when the coolant temperature at start is at or below this; a warmer (hot restart) start goes straight to normal running. Lower it to skip the warm-up phases on more starts. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Start Coolant Minimum
table.description: The cold-start sequence runs only when the coolant temperature at start is at or above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence Cranking Time Limit
table.description: If cranking lasts this long, the cold-start sequence is abandoned and the engine goes to normal running mode. Counter units (passes). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence IAT Maximum
table.description: The cold-start sequence runs only when intake air temperature is at or below this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Sequence IAT Minimum
table.description: The cold-start sequence runs only when intake air temperature is at or above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Phase Maximum Time
table.description: Longest time the first warm-up phase (combustion mode 1) may last before the ECU moves to catalyst-heating phase 2. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Phase Torque Maximum
table.description: The first warm-up phase ends (moves to catalyst-heating phase 2) when engine torque reaches this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Phase Pedal Maximum
table.description: The first warm-up phase ends when the accelerator reaches this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Phase Load Minimum
table.description: The first warm-up phase ends when load (whole %) is below this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Phase Load Maximum
table.description: The first warm-up phase ends when load (whole %) is above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Coolant Maximum
table.description: Highest coolant temperature at which stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2) is allowed; outside the window the ECU goes to phase 2 (mode 3). Set below Catalyst Heating Coolant Minimum to never enter mode 2 (mode 2 is also blocked while Catalyst Heating Minimum RPM is above the rev limit). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Coolant Minimum
table.description: Lowest coolant temperature at which stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2) is allowed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Minimum RPM
table.description: Engine speed needed to enter and stay in stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2). Set above the rev limit, mode 2 is never entered and the start goes from mode 1 to catalyst-heating phase 2 (mode 3). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Progress Maximum
table.description: Stratified catalyst heating (mode 2) is entered only while the spark torque share is at or below this, i.e. with a large retard requested. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Vehicle Speed Maximum
table.description: Stratified catalyst heating (mode 2) only while vehicle speed is at or below this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Torque Maximum
table.description: Stratified catalyst heating (mode 2) only while engine torque is below this; it ends once torque reaches it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Maximum Time
table.description: Longest time stratified catalyst heating (mode 2) may last before phase 2. Counter units (passes). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Accumulated Limit
table.description: Mode 2 ends when an internal accumulated value reaches this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume RPM Adder (Coolant)
table.description: Added to the idle target to set the rpm at which the decel fuel cut ends (and, 200 rpm higher, where it starts), by coolant. Raising it probably ends the cut at a higher rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay
table.description: Delay between the closed-pedal decel fuel cut condition being met and cylinders starting to be cut, by coolant and rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume RPM Adder (A/C, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate A/C resume-rpm adder for the decel fuel cut, by an unidentified CAN-derived value. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 1)
table.description: Decel fuel cut cylinder staging for gear 1. Row = engine speed band (1: below 1450, 2: below 2000, 3: below 3000, 4: below 4000, 5: below 5000, 6: from 5000 rpm); column n = how long after the cut condition starts n cylinders are cut. The ECU multiplies each value by a second per-gear factor table that is not in this definition yet, so the values are relative (raw). Values should rise along each row. Gear 0 uses the gear 1 table. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 2)
table.description: Decel fuel cut cylinder staging for gear 2. Row = engine speed band (1: below 1450, 2: below 2000, 3: below 3000, 4: below 4000, 5: below 5000, 6: from 5000 rpm); column n = how long after the cut condition starts n cylinders are cut. table.description: Decel fuel cut cylinder staging for gear 6. Row = engine speed band (1: below 1450, 2: below 2000, 3: below 3000, 4: below 4000, 5: below 5000, 6: from 5000 rpm); column n = how long after the cut condition starts n cylinders are cut. The ECU multiplies each value by a second per-gear factor table that is not in this definition yet, so the values are relative (raw). Values should rise along each row. Gear 0 uses the gear 1 table. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Alternate Set)
table.description: Replaces the gear tables when a pass counter exceeds a calibration value; with that value at its maximum it is never used. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Neutral)
table.description: Decel fuel cut staging in neutral: all four stage boundaries come from this, by vehicle speed (raw, relative units as the gear tables). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro)
table.description: Air density by intake temperature and barometric pressure, used to compute purge flow capacity. Exact physics: normally no reason to edit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Purge Rate Cut Recovery Step (Off-Idle)
table.description: How fast a purge cut is released, pedal pressed, by how much margin the closed-loop correction has above its lower limit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Purge Rate Ramp Step (Off-Idle)
table.description: How much the purge rate rises per learning update once vapour concentration has been learned, pedal pressed, by learned concentration. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Purge Learning Weight (Purge Flow)
table.description: Weight by purge flow on how much each sample moves the learned vapour concentration (255 = x1.0). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Purge Learning Weight (Trim Deviation)
table.description: Weight by the size of the closed-loop correction on the vapour concentration learning (255 = x1.0); a dead band so small trim noise does not move it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Purge Rate Cut Recovery Step (Idle)
table.description: How fast a purge cut is released at idle (pedal released). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released)
table.description: Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing (EGR Active, TGV Open)
table.description: Base (upper-limit) ignition timing map used while the pedal is pressed, EGR is active and the TGVs are open (part-throttle cruising). The ECU fires the lower of this map and Primary Ignition plus EGR advance, knock correction advance and fine learning, so raising cells adds timing only where this map is the lower one. The ECU blends the four base maps: TGV open against TGV closed by TGV opening, then the EGR-off pair against the EGR-active pair by the current EGR rate relative to its maximum (all EGR-active at full EGR). Edit matching cells in all four to change timing regardless of EGR and TGV state. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing (EGR Active, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (upper-limit) ignition timing map used while the pedal is pressed, EGR is active and the TGVs are closed. The ECU fires the lower of this map and Primary Ignition plus knock correction advance and fine learning (then feedback knock correction and retards apply), so raising cells adds timing only where this map is the lower one. One of four base maps selected by EGR and TGV state; that the switching module is EGR is inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open)
table.description: Base (upper-limit) ignition timing map for pedal pressed, EGR off and TGVs open, which covers wide-open throttle and high rpm. The ECU fires the lower of this map and Primary Ignition plus knock correction advance and fine learning. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing Advance Rate (mode change)
table.description: Limit on how fast base timing may advance per pass (the highest value means no limit). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Base Timing Advance Rate
table.description: Limit on how fast base timing may advance per pass (the highest value means no limit). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Minimum Ignition Timing (Coolant)
table.description: Lowest timing the ECU will fire, by coolant temperature, used with the pedal pressed and the throttle between about 3 % and 46 % open; otherwise Minimum Ignition Timing applies. Lowering it allows more retard. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Ignition Dwell Time
table.description: Coil charge (dwell) time in milliseconds by rpm and battery voltage, used whenever the engine runs. More dwell gives a stronger spark but heats the coils. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Minimum Ignition Timing
table.description: Lowest timing the ECU will ever fire when Minimum Ignition Timing (Coolant) does not apply. Final timing is never allowed below this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Maximum Ignition Timing
table.description: Upper limit on fired ignition timing. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Timing Request Enrichment Retard
table.description: Retard ramped into the timing request while open-loop power enrichment is active, by load and rpm. The ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and request + knock advance. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Closed)
table.description: Timing added to base timing on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, for the TGV-closed side, blended with the TGV Open table by how far the TGVs are open. Active above about 800 rpm. Keep consistent with Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Temperature Timing Compensation Reference Temperature
table.description: Intake temperature timing compensation: Reference Temperature by engine speed and load. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Temperature Timing Compensation Weight
table.description: Intake temperature timing compensation: Weight by engine speed and load. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open)
table.description: Timing added to base timing on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, for the TGV-open side; scaled by Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open) and blended with the TGV Closed table by how far the TGVs are open. Active above about 800 rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Closed)
table.description: Share of the TGV-closed coolant timing compensation that applies, by engine speed and load. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open)
table.description: Percentage (by rpm and load) of Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open) actually applied. Lower values reduce the cold-engine timing correction in that area. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max A (TGV Closed)
table.description: First part of the knock correction advance (timing added as DAM rises), by rpm and load, for TGVs closed; blended with the TGV Open table and scaled by KCA DAM Curve A. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, not to the Base Timing map: the ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and Primary + knock advance + fine learning, so raising it adds timing only where that sum is still below Base Timing. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max A (TGV Open)
table.description: First part of the knock correction advance (timing added as DAM rises), by rpm and load, for TGVs open; blended with the TGV Closed table and scaled by KCA DAM Curve A. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, not to the Base Timing map: the ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and Primary + knock advance + fine learning, so raising it adds timing only where that sum is still below Base Timing. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max B (TGV Closed)
table.description: Second part of the knock correction advance, by rpm and load, for TGVs closed. Like part A it raises the Primary Ignition side of the timing limit and can never push fired timing above the Base Timing map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max B (TGV Open)
table.description: Second part of the knock correction advance, by rpm and load, for TGVs open. The total available advance is Max A plus Max B; it raises the Primary Ignition side of the timing limit and can never push fired timing above the Base Timing map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance DAM Curve A
table.description: Knock correction advance multiplier curve A by DAM. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance DAM Curve B
table.description: Knock correction advance multiplier curve B by DAM. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: DAM Step Gain (FLKC Cell)

scaling.units: FLKC cell (5 x rpm range + load range)

table.description: How strongly each fine-knock-learning step moves DAM, per FLKC learning cell (index = 5 x rpm range + load range, 0-34; index 0 is the lowest rpm and load cell). Larger values make DAM move faster when the ECU learns knock in that cell; 0 means that cell never moves DAM. Purpose is inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fine Learning Counted-Cell Threshold
table.description: Fine learning knock correction: Counted-Cell Threshold. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: DAM Initial Value
table.description: The DAM the ECU starts from after a reset of the learned values (battery disconnect or a scan-tool reset). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: DAM Step
table.description: How far DAM moves per learning step up or down; halved each time the direction reverses. When 0, DAM moves only by DAM Step Gain (FLKC Cell). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 6)
table.description: Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires (variant with an extra internal condition set). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Knock, State 7)
table.description: Timing pulled by feedback knock correction for each knock event detected above Knock Threshold, in the second main-knock case (an extra internal condition is set). Applied once per combustion event. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description: Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Knock, State 0x0E)
table.description: Timing pulled by feedback knock correction for each knock event detected above Knock Threshold, in the main knock case. Applied once per combustion event, to all cylinders (there is no per-cylinder knock retard). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Maximum Retard
table.description: Largest amount of timing feedback knock correction can pull. The live knock retard never goes below minus this value, and it applies to all cylinders at once. Raising it allows more protective retard. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Recovery Step (State 0x0F)
table.description: Timing given back by feedback knock correction per combustion event after a long knock-free stretch (about 100 events since the last knock). Larger values recover faster. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Recovery Step
table.description: Timing given back by feedback knock correction per combustion event in the non-knock states other than normal knock-free running: when rpm is outside the FBKC window (for example below FBKC Window RPM Minimum), in the closed-pedal / low-load state, and in a few other special states. Inside the window, after knock stops the correction is held for 100 knock-free events and then recovered by FBKC Recovery Step (State 0x0F), not by this value. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Feedback Knock Recovery Knock-Free Count
table.description: Feedback knock correction setting. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Window RPM Minimum
table.description: Lower rpm limit for feedback knock correction: below it no new knock retard is taken, and any existing knock retard is given back by FBKC Recovery Step each combustion event. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FBKC Window RPM Maximum
table.description: Upper rpm limit for feedback knock correction. Above it the current knock retard is held: no new retard and no recovery. Raise this if you raise the rev limit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fine Learning Maximum (Advance)
table.description: Fine learning knock correction: Maximum (Advance). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fine Learning Minimum (Retard)
table.description: Fine learning knock correction: Minimum (Retard). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fine Learning Advance Step
table.description: Fine learning knock correction: Advance Step. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fine Learning Retard Step (State 8)
table.description: Fine learning knock correction: Retard Step (State 8). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fine Learning Retard Step (States 9-11)
table.description: Fine learning knock correction: Retard Step (States 9-11). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 1
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 2
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 3
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 2
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 3
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 4
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Event Fine Learning Correction Hysteresis
table.description: Once summing, fine learning knock correction must recover this far above the threshold to stop. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Event Fine Learning Correction Threshold
table.description: Knocking cylinders are summed while fine learning knock correction is at or below this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 1)
table.description: Knock detection threshold for cylinder 1 by engine speed and load: knock is flagged when this cylinder's knock intensity reaches it. Raise it and less is called knock; lower it and more is. Units are the ECU's raw intensity counts. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 1, Retard Condition)
table.description: Knock threshold for cylinder 1 used instead of Knock Threshold (Cylinder 1) only when timing is retarded past a set limit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 2)
table.description: Knock detection threshold for cylinder 2 by engine speed and load: knock is flagged when this cylinder's knock intensity reaches it. Raise it and less is called knock; lower it and more is. Units are the ECU's raw intensity counts. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 2, Retard Condition)
table.description: Knock threshold for cylinder 2 used instead of Knock Threshold (Cylinder 2) only when timing is retarded past a set limit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 3)
table.description: Knock detection threshold for cylinder 3 by engine speed and load: knock is flagged when this cylinder's knock intensity reaches it. Raise it and less is called knock; lower it and more is. Units are the ECU's raw intensity counts. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 3, Retard Condition)
table.description: Knock threshold for cylinder 3 used instead of Knock Threshold (Cylinder 3) only when timing is retarded past a set limit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 4)
table.description: Knock detection threshold for cylinder 4 by engine speed and load: knock is flagged when this cylinder's knock intensity reaches it. Raise it and less is called knock; lower it and more is. Units are the ECU's raw intensity counts. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Cylinder 4, Retard Condition)
table.description: Knock threshold for cylinder 4 used instead of Knock Threshold (Cylinder 4) only when timing is retarded past a set limit. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Cylinder 1, Channel 1)
table.description: Knock signal processing for cylinder 1, channel 1 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor), by engine speed and load. When the knock window changes, this step shifts the channel's background reference so the change does not read as knock. Larger = more shift. Edit the cylinders together and only with logging. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Flag Gate Threshold
table.description: Second threshold in knock detection, by engine speed and load. For the firing cylinder, the ECU adds the three largest of its eight knock-channel values; when that sum is above this table the cylinder's gate opens, and only then can the secondary knock flag be set (it also needs the intensity above that cylinder's Knock Threshold). Raw units (the channel values are not yet confirmed to share Knock Threshold's scale). Raising it makes the secondary knock flag harder to trigger. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no table of this name. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Reduction Spark Retard
table.description: Turns a torque or efficiency shortfall back into spark retard on base timing. Besides torque reduction, it is how the ECU pulls fired timing down to Primary Ignition (or the closed-pedal target) plus knock correction advance where that is below Base Timing, so it must stay the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard; don't edit one without the other. Not used in the rev/overboost-cut states. It holds the same data as Catalyst Heating Spark Retard (Phase 2): editing one edits the other. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Timing Advance Term A (EGR Timing Advance) 1
table.description: Timing advance term 1 by engine speed and load in the EGR timing path. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.description: Timing advance term 2 by engine speed and load in the EGR timing path. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.description: Timing advance term 4 by engine speed and load in the EGR timing path. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Ignition Timing Per-Cylinder Trim 4
table.description: Per-cylinder ignition trim map 4 (the cylinder each map belongs to has not been read). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Hold (RPM)
table.description: When the A/C compressor switches off near standstill, the ECU retards timing 5 degrees for this many combustion events (one per 180 degrees of crank rotation), by rpm, then ramps the retard out. Probably smooths the idle load change. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Combustion Mode Factor
table.description: Scales the surge damping timing correction by combustion mode (0 = off, 1.0 = full). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used below 200 km/h between about 3900 and 6375 rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used from 200 to 250 km/h, between about 3900 and 6375 rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum
table.description: Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle after the stab must be at or above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum
table.description: Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle before the stab must be below this. Together with Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum it defines a big low-to-high throttle jump. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle
table.description: Tip-in classification by rpm: once the pedal has been pressed for a short while and throttle is at or above this, the tip-in class is held rather than reassigned to classes 2/3 or dropped back to 1. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic)
table.description: Alternate A/C-switch timing retard amount, by an unidentified input. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (From 200 km/h)

table.name: Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Start (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Phase time of the tip-in lash retard (Drive Mode 1, Default), in passes counted from the tip-in: Start. Before Start the retard is zero. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Reference
table.description: Internal reference of the tip-in lash retard (the torque reference normalises the torque request between the Low and High Torque maps). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Tip-Out Timing Retard
table.description: Timing pulled, by gear and manifold pressure, when rpm rises shortly after lifting off the pedal on a warm engine above walking speed; probably damps driveline shunt or coasting downshift jolts. Latched on the event and removed at once afterwards. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard A (Coolant at Start)
table.description: Second post-start retard term by coolant at start. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard B (Coolant at Start)
table.description: Timing retard after a normal start, by the coolant temperature at start, at low rpm. It is scaled by its baro, torque and load factors, held and ramped. Negative = retard. The post-start role is inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard B (Coolant)
table.description: Version of Post-Start Timing Retard B by present coolant temperature, used while a start flag selects it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard A Baro Factor
table.description: Scales post-start timing retard A by Baro (255 = full). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard B Baro Factor
table.description: Scales post-start timing retard B by Baro (255 = full). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard A Torque Factor
table.description: Scales post-start timing retard A by Torque (255 = full). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard B Torque Factor
table.description: Scales post-start timing retard B by Torque (255 = full). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Timing Retard Load Factor

table.name: Surge Damping Phase Factor RPM Split

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation
table.description: Timing added with the pedal released on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, scaled by Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier. Adds to the pedal-released base timing and the closed-pedal target. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback) (Idle State Group 1)
table.description: AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1). Group 1 is used in the idle controller's states 1-4 and 6: an override flag; out of neutral without a valid received idle-speed request; moving (4 km/h or more); stopped with engine speed at or above the received request; and above it in neutral. Group 2 covers the rest: the default state (neutral without a valid request) and stopped below the request. On the manual car the request comes over CAN, probably from a transmission controller it does not have (inferred), so in practice group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Mode 1 is combustion mode 1, the first warm-up phase after start (inferred: the start spark targets are chosen by combustion mode, as on FA20). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback) (Idle State Group 2)
table.description: AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1). Group 2 is used in the idle controller's default state (neutral without a valid received idle-speed request) and while stopped below that request; Group 1 covers the others. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 2 is in practice neutral and group 1 out of neutral. Mode 1 is combustion mode 1, the first warm-up phase after start (inferred: the start spark targets are chosen by combustion mode, as on FA20). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation by rpm (1.0 = full amount). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1). Mode 1 is combustion mode 1, the first warm-up phase after start (inferred: the start spark targets are chosen by combustion mode, as on FA20). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Map
Engine speed (median of three crank captures)

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Map (Alternate)

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Ceiling RPM Term

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Ceiling Torque Term

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Ceiling Coolant Term
table.description: Added to Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Ceiling. 0 inside the window where the resume limit applies, 63.5 degrees (no limit) outside it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Ignition Feedback (RPM Error, Warm-Up Modes)

table.name: Idle Ignition Feedback (RPM Error)

table.name: Idle Ignition Feedback (RPM Change)
table.description: Timing correction at idle by how fast engine speed is moving away from its filtered value (a damping term), by target idle. Positive = advance. Normal running; works with the RPM Error map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Boost IAT Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the boost target by intake air temperature (1.00 = no change). Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Target Boost IAT Multiplier (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Target Boost Baro Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the boost target by engine speed and barometric pressure (1.00 = no change). Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Target Boost Baro Multiplier (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Target Boost Baro Multiplier (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Target Boost Baro Multiplier. The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Target Boost Baro Multiplier, or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Actuator Target Speed
table.description: How fast the actuator is asked to move, by how far it is from the commanded position (raw units). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Motor Feed-Forward Duty
table.description: Motor drive for the requested actuator speed, before the position feedback. Positive opens the wastegate. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Position Feed-Forward
table.description: Base wastegate position by engine speed and boost target, before feedback. 0% is closed on its seat; larger is more open. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Position IAT Compensation
table.description: Scales the feed-forward opening by engine speed and intake air temperature (1.00 = no change). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Position Baro Compensation
table.description: Scales the feed-forward opening by engine speed and barometric pressure (1.00 = no change). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Learned Seat Maximum
table.description: Highest value the learned closed (seat) position may take. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Learned Seat Minimum
table.description: Lowest value the learned closed (seat) position may take. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Motor Duty Maximum
table.description: Largest opening drive to the wastegate motor. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Wastegate Motor Duty Minimum
table.description: Largest closing drive to the wastegate motor. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: P0244 Wastegate Position Error Limit
table.description: Position error (commanded minus measured) that counts towards the wastegate actuator fault. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: P0244 Wastegate Position Error Passes
table.description: How long the position error must last before the wastegate actuator fault is set (passes). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Boost Feed-Forward-Only Threshold IAT Factor
table.description: Scales the feed-forward-only threshold by engine speed and intake air temperature (1.00 = no change). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Boost Proportional (Wastegate Position)
table.description: Wastegate position change in proportion to boost error (target minus actual). Negative closes the wastegate. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Boost Integral Step (Wastegate Position)

table.name: Boost Feed-Forward-Only Threshold

table.name: Boost Feed-Forward-Only Threshold Baro Factor
table.description: Scales the feed-forward-only threshold by engine speed and barometric pressure (1.00 = no change). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Boost Integral Minimum (Wastegate Position)
table.description: Largest closing the boost integral can add. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Boost Integral Maximum (Wastegate Position)
table.description: Largest opening the boost integral can add. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Boost Feedback Maximum (Wastegate Position)

table.name: Boost Feedback Minimum (Wastegate Position)

Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.
