table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the Stage 1 tip-in rise rate by pedal position, so harder tip-ins build torque faster. Applies to all drive modes. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the Stage 2 tip-in rise rate by pedal position, so harder tip-ins build torque faster. Applies to all drive modes. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time
table.description: Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time stopped with the pedal released. Its axis input is not identified (raw). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Low-Speed Time
table.description: Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time the car has been stopped. Its axis input is not identified (raw). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7)
table.description: Requested torque by accelerator pedal and engine speed for drive mode 7, which the ECU selects when the drive-mode value it receives over CAN is 7. This mode has no per-gear set: the manual car uses this map directly. The manual car probably stays in drive mode 1 (inferred). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: the smoothing only acts when the request is below it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step A (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step A, the fast fall rate per 10 ms, for the normal set. Raise for quicker tip-out, lower for smoother. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Threshold (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Threshold, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: where the fast fall (Step A) switches to the slow fall (Step B). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step B (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step B, the slow fall rate per 10 ms below the Threshold, for the normal set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag): smoothing only acts below it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step A (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step A, the fast fall rate per 10 ms, for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag). Raise for quicker tip-out, lower for smoother. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Threshold (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Threshold, by gear and rpm, for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag): where the fast fall (Step A) switches to the slow fall (Step B). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step B (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step B, the slow fall rate per 10 ms below the Threshold, for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing: when the torque request drops, the target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms down to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling for the low-speed set (below about 4 km/h), used in place of Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Normal): the smoothing only acts when the request is below it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step A (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step A, the fast fall rate per 10 ms, for the set used below about 4 km/h. Raise for quicker tip-out, lower for smoother. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Threshold (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Threshold for the set used below about 4 km/h. In 1st gear it is 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) up to 3600 rpm and 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) above, and the 1st-gear low-speed steps are unlimited, so 1st gear gets practically no smoothing below 4 km/h. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step B (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step B, the slow fall rate per 10 ms below the Threshold, for the set used below about 4 km/h. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Shaping Threshold
table.description: Torque by rpm below which the requested torque is used directly. Above it the ECU follows the rise/fall-shaped (rate-limited) torque, but never less than this curve. Raising it makes larger torque changes respond without smoothing; lowering it smooths more of the range. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Shaping Threshold B
table.description: Second threshold in the same torque-shaping decision as Torque Shaping Threshold. Keep the two together. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch
table.description: Switch byte. Bit 3 (value 8) on: in drive modes 1-3 the manual car uses the per-gear requested torque maps (Neutral, Gear 1-6) instead of each mode's base map. Off: the base maps. The other bits of this byte switch unrelated functions: change only bit 3. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Requested Torque Cap (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Upper limit on the requested torque from the drive mode 1 (Default) maps. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Requested Torque Cap (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Upper limit on the requested torque from the drive mode 2 (Sport) maps. The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Maximum Torque (DAM)
table.description: Maximum target torque by DAM (knock learning) and rpm, in the same lowest-wins limit as Maximum Torque (IAT). Losing DAM lowers the torque target and so the boost target. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Maximum Torque (DAM) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Maximum Torque (IAT)
table.description: Maximum target torque by rpm and intake air temperature. The ECU uses the lowest of this, Maximum Torque (DAM) and other limits, and the result drives the boost target. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Maximum Torque (IAT) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Event)
table.description: Torque ceiling while the knock-event detector has tripped, by engine speed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Event, Alternate)
table.description: The same ceiling, used instead when an ECU flag selects it (not identified). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Maximum Torque (DAM) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Maximum Torque (DAM). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Maximum Torque (DAM), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Maximum Torque (IAT) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Maximum Torque (IAT). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Maximum Torque (IAT), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1)
table.description: Throttle-side torque cap while the rev limiter is cutting fuel, or during an overboost cut above 256 kPa absolute: the throttle closes toward it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 2)
table.description: Second throttle-side cap of the rev/overboost cut. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base)
table.description: Throttle-side torque cap by rpm used only during the rev or overboost cut when neither stage applies. It does not limit torque in normal driving, so raising it gives no extra power. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Torque Limit A
table.description: Maximum engine torque by engine speed while a particular fault flag is set; without the fault it has no effect. The ECU uses the lowest of the four fail-safe limits (A-D) and the torque request. Which faults set each flag is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Torque Limit B
table.description: Maximum engine torque by engine speed while a particular fault flag is set; without the fault it has no effect. The ECU uses the lowest of the four fail-safe limits (A-D) and the torque request. Which faults set each flag is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Torque Limit C
table.description: Maximum engine torque by engine speed while a particular fault flag is set; without the fault it has no effect. The ECU uses the lowest of the four fail-safe limits (A-D) and the torque request. Which faults set each flag is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Torque Limit D
table.description: Maximum engine torque by engine speed while a particular fault flag is set; without the fault it has no effect. The ECU uses the lowest of the four fail-safe limits (A-D) and the torque request. Which faults set each flag is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Torque Limit A (CAN Flag Set)
table.description: Maximum torque by engine speed while knock condition A is flagged by the knock detection (A has priority, then B, then C), used when a flag received over CAN is Set. The applied limit moves toward it at Knock Torque Limit Ramp Rate. Which knock condition each letter is, and what the CAN flag means, are not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Knock Torque Limit A (CAN Flag Clear)
table.description: Maximum torque by engine speed while knock condition A is flagged by the knock detection (A has priority, then B, then C), used when a flag received over CAN is Clear. The applied limit moves toward it at Knock Torque Limit Ramp Rate. Which knock condition each letter is, and what the CAN flag means, are not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Knock Torque Limit B (CAN Flag Set)
table.description: Maximum torque by engine speed while knock condition B is flagged by the knock detection (A has priority, then B, then C), used when a flag received over CAN is Set. The applied limit moves toward it at Knock Torque Limit Ramp Rate. Which knock condition each letter is, and what the CAN flag means, are not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Knock Torque Limit B (CAN Flag Clear)
table.description: Maximum torque by engine speed while knock condition B is flagged by the knock detection (A has priority, then B, then C), used when a flag received over CAN is Clear. The applied limit moves toward it at Knock Torque Limit Ramp Rate. Which knock condition each letter is, and what the CAN flag means, are not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Knock Torque Limit C (CAN Flag Set)
table.description: Maximum torque by engine speed while knock condition C is flagged by the knock detection (A has priority, then B, then C), used when a flag received over CAN is Set. The applied limit moves toward it at Knock Torque Limit Ramp Rate. Which knock condition each letter is, and what the CAN flag means, are not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Knock Torque Limit C (CAN Flag Clear)
table.description: Maximum torque by engine speed while knock condition C is flagged by the knock detection (A has priority, then B, then C), used when a flag received over CAN is Clear. The applied limit moves toward it at Knock Torque Limit Ramp Rate. Which knock condition each letter is, and what the CAN flag means, are not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Knock Torque Limit Ramp Rate
table.description: How fast the applied knock torque limit moves toward its target, per pass, by engine speed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)
table.description: Stage 1 of the throttle cap holds above this rpm. Set it to your rev limit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM
table.description: Set it to your rev limit with the other Rev Limit rpm values. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM
table.description: Fuel returns once rpm falls to this and boost is below Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit Hysteresis
table.description: How far rpm must fall below an active fail-safe rev limit before fuel returns. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit Minimum Above Idle Target
table.description: A fail-safe rev limit is never set lower than the idle target plus this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (1 Cylinder)
table.description: When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (2 Cylinders)
table.description: Below this share of current torque, two cylinders in four are cut. Also sets the second decel fuel cut stage. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (3 Cylinders)
table.description: Below this share of current torque, three cylinders in four are cut. Also sets the third decel fuel cut stage. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (4 Cylinders)
table.description: Below this share of current torque all cylinders are cut. The rev limiter asks for zero torque, so it always cuts all four. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Rail Pressure Fault)
table.description: Rev limit used only while a fuel-rail pressure fault is active: above it fuel to all cylinders is cut. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Injector Driver Fault)
table.description: Rev limit used only while an injector-driver fault has put the fuel system in its low-pressure fail-safe: above it fuel to all cylinders is cut. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Fault C)
table.description: Fail-safe rev limit tied to a fault flag that nothing sets in this software. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Pedal Limits Disable
table.description: Switch that disables the pedal limits. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut RPM
table.description: At or above this rpm, once the rev limit has started, every injector is cut on every firing (a hard fuel cut). Keep it equal to Rev Limit RPM; set higher, the range between them gets only the throttle cap, probably a softer limit. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold
table.description: Vehicle speed above which the rev-limit fuel cut uses the Stage 1 / Stage 2 rpm values instead of the Full Cut pair. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis
table.description: Extra speed needed above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold before the switch. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit RPM
table.description: The rev limit: above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Reset RPM
table.description: End of the rev-limit state: the throttle cap stays until rpm falls to this and boost is below Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP, while fuel already returns at Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM. Keep it about 100 rpm below Rev Limit RPM. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP
table.description: The rev-limit fuel cut and state cannot end while manifold pressure is at or above this, even below their reset rpm. Raise it if you want the cut to release on rpm alone at high boost. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP
table.description: During a rev or overboost cut, manifold pressure above which the stage 1 throttle cap is used. It does not start a cut by itself. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 Reset MAP
table.description: Stage 1 throttle cap stays on while manifold pressure is above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 2 Hold MAP
table.description: Stage 2 throttle cap stays on while manifold pressure is above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit
table.description: Vehicle speed limiter. It needs this speed, Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM and Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed to act, and then cuts fuel to all cylinders without closing the throttle. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Offset
table.description: Subtracted from Vehicle Speed Limit to give the speed where the limiter state starts; it is not a release hysteresis. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM
table.description: The speed limiter only starts at or above this engine speed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description: Speed at which the active speed limiter cuts fuel to all cylinders; without it the limiter does nothing. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
table.description: How far speed must fall below Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed before the fuel cut ends. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
table.description: The speed limiter cannot release while manifold pressure is above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis on Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Monitor Fault Mode
table.description: Selects when the ECU's torque monitor raises its fault. The monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from the (Monitor) copies of the requested torque, reference torque and boost tables and checks the engine's torque against it in two channels. 1 = fault when channel 1 trips, 2 = channel 2, 3 = only when both trip, 4 = when either trips, 0 (or any value above 4) = never. When the fault is raised the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). This value is the only route from the check to that reaction (the raw check results are only kept for diagnosis), so at 0 the (Monitor) copies have no effect. 0 also removes the ECU's guard against a torque request it did not intend, and it has not been tested on a car. The safer way to change torque is to keep every (Monitor) copy identical to its main table. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Request Limit (Coolant)
table.description: Upper limit, by coolant temperature, on the idle air request (probably from idle speed control) before it is converted to throttle area. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit Baro Factor
table.description: Barometric factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Air Spark Compensation Limit
table.description: Caps, by actual ignition timing, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded timing. Shares data with two other entries: editing one edits all three. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Limit (Rail Pressure Deviation)
table.description: Throttle opening cap by rpm for a rail-pressure-deviation fault mode. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Request to Throttle Area
table.description: Converts the idle air request into throttle area, which is added to the pedal-driven opening and sets the idle throttle floor. Edit together with Idle Air Request to Throttle Area (Monitor). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Area from Opening
table.description: Converts a throttle opening (%) into throttle area; the exact inverse of Throttle Opening (Required Area). Also gives the required area during cranking. Keep the two consistent; leave alone unless the throttle body changes. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open). Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Throttle Area from Opening (Zero-Opening Copy).

table.name: Throttle Opening (Required Area)
table.description: Converts the required throttle area into commanded throttle opening (%). It is the exact inverse of Throttle Area from Opening; keep the two consistent, and edit Throttle Opening (Monitor) too. Leave alone unless the throttle body changes. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open). Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Throttle Opening (Idle Area).

table.name: Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque
table.description: Torque by rpm that counts as 100 % in the Throttle Opening from Target Torque maps: at or above it they give wide-open throttle. Raise it together with Full-Load Reference Brake Torque for a higher-torque tune. Edit together with Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque (Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Reference Torque.

table.name: Throttle Command Term
table.description: Has no effect: the ECU calculates a value from it that nothing reads. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Command Rate Term
table.description: Has no effect: the ECU calculates a value from it that nothing reads. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Start Throttle Opening Add (Coolant)
table.description: Extra throttle opening during engine start (cranking, car stopped), by coolant temperature. Edit together with Start Throttle Opening Add (Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open)
table.description: This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs open and no EGR; probably the table a warm car mostly uses at part load. Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, EGR)
table.description: This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs open and EGR active (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, EGR, Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed)
table.description: This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs closed and no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, EGR)
table.description: This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Used with the TGVs closed and EGR active (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, EGR, Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed)
table.description: This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Probably used while cruise control is active; TGVs closed, no EGR. Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed, Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed, EGR)
table.description: This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Probably used while cruise control is active; TGVs closed, EGR active. Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed, EGR, Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Open)
table.description: Throttle opening by engine speed and target torque (as a fraction of Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque) while cruise control is active, TGV open, no EGR. Blended with the EGR version by EGR rate and with the TGV-closed cruise pair by TGV opening. FA24 has no published table of this name. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Open, EGR)
table.description: This is where part-throttle feel is set: the commanded throttle opening is essentially this map (by rpm and target torque) plus the idle air. Probably used while cruise control is active; TGVs open, EGR active. Edit together with Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Open, EGR, Monitor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Torque Request Cap
table.description: Cap on the torque request (plus engine losses) that the throttle model works from. Raise it for high-torque tunes. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Ignition Efficiency vs Retard
table.description: How much torque the engine loses when timing is retarded from base timing (1.0 = no loss). The torque model uses it, and together with its inverse, Torque Reduction Spark Retard, it also decides how far the fired timing is pulled down toward Primary Ignition plus knock advance. Leave alone, or edit together with its inverse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model. Group 1 is used in the idle controller's states 1-4 and 6: an override flag; out of neutral without a valid received idle-speed request; moving (4 km/h or more); stopped with engine speed at or above the received request; and above it in neutral. Group 2 covers the rest: the default state (neutral without a valid request) and stopped below the request. On the manual car the request comes over CAN, probably from a transmission controller it does not have (inferred), so in practice group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model. Group 2 is used in the idle controller's default state (neutral without a valid received idle-speed request) and while stopped below that request; Group 1 covers the others. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 2 is in practice neutral and group 1 out of neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Group 2 is used in the idle controller's default state (neutral without a valid received idle-speed request) and while stopped below that request; Group 1 covers the others. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 2 is in practice neutral and group 1 out of neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Start Value (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of Spark Compensation Event Start Value, used in the idle controller's state group 1 (some of its operating states; the plain table is used in the others). Leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Start Value
table.description: Value the torque model's spark compensation jumps to at the start of an event (the trigger is not identified), by rpm and coolant, before decaying back. Leave alone unless you know the model. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Response Filter Weight (Throttle Closing)
table.description: How quickly the torque model expects delivered torque to follow after the throttle closes quickly (larger = faster), by rpm. Part of the modelled torque used for spark compensation. Leave alone unless you know the model. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Response Filter Weight (Throttle Opening)
table.description: How quickly the torque model expects delivered torque to follow after the throttle opens quickly (larger = faster), by rpm. Part of the modelled torque used for spark compensation. Leave alone unless you know the model. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Torque IAT Factor
table.description: Intake-temperature correction on the full-load reference torque (and on an upper torque ceiling). Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Full-Load Reference Torque IAT Factor (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Full-Load Reference Brake Torque
table.description: Full-load torque by rpm (density corrected) that the throttle/boost model divides every request by. It does not change part-throttle opening; it moves the full-load handover, target MAP and torque limits (raising it lowers target MAP for the same torque). Keep it equal to Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque from 2000 rpm, and edit the (Monitor) copy too. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Full-Load Reference Brake Torque (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Full-Load Reference Torque Loss
table.description: Engine loss torque by rpm added to Full-Load Reference Brake Torque to give the full-load reference the whole throttle/boost model divides by. Probably a mechanical loss at full load (about the same as Friction and Pumping Torque Loss there). Edit the (Monitor) copy too. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Full-Load Reference Torque Loss (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Hold Time
table.description: Maximum length of a spark-compensation event in the torque model (the event's trigger is not identified). Leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Decay Step (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of Spark Compensation Event Decay Step, used in the idle controller's state group 1 (some of its operating states; the plain table is used in the others). Leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Decay Step
table.description: How fast the spark-compensation event value decays back per 10 ms. Leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Initial Hold (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of Spark Compensation Event Initial Hold, used in the idle controller's state group 1 (some of its operating states; the plain table is used in the others). Leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Spark Compensation Event Initial Hold
table.description: How long the torque model holds the spark-compensation start value before it begins to decay. Leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Torque IAT Factor (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Full-Load Reference Torque IAT Factor. The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Full-Load Reference Torque IAT Factor, or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Torque Loss (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Full-Load Reference Torque Loss. The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Full-Load Reference Torque Loss, or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Brake Torque (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Full-Load Reference Brake Torque. The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Full-Load Reference Brake Torque, or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Path B, Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used in another phase after a combustion-mode change. Leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used after a combustion-mode change until timing reaches the spark target. Leave alone. Group 1 is used in the idle controller's states 1-4 and 6: an override flag; out of neutral without a valid received idle-speed request; moving (4 km/h or more); stopped with engine speed at or above the received request; and above it in neutral. Group 2 covers the rest: the default state (neutral without a valid request) and stopped below the request. On the manual car the request comes over CAN, probably from a transmission controller it does not have (inferred), so in practice group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Rate Limit (EGR Low)
table.description: Largest drop in target torque per pass when the request falls, by gear and engine speed. The ECU blends the Low, Middle and High tables by an EGR rate measure (breakpoints near 10, 20 and 25 % EGR). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Rate Limit (EGR Middle)
table.description: Largest drop in target torque per pass when the request falls, by gear and engine speed. The ECU blends the Low, Middle and High tables by an EGR rate measure (breakpoints near 10, 20 and 25 % EGR). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Rate Limit (EGR High)
table.description: Largest drop in target torque per pass when the request falls, by gear and engine speed. The ECU blends the Low, Middle and High tables by an EGR rate measure (breakpoints near 10, 20 and 25 % EGR). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Fraction from Throttle Area
table.description: Share of the full-load reference torque reachable at a given effective throttle area (throttle plus idle air), by rpm, as a fraction (1.0 = full-load torque). The torque model reads it twice: with the throttle area at zero opening, giving the minimum torque with the throttle closed, and with the area at the commanded opening, giving the torque that opening delivers. Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Torque Fraction from Throttle Area (Commanded Opening).

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed)
table.description: Volumetric efficiency by rpm and manifold pressure; feeds the ECU's air-mass model that defines engine load. The ECU blends the TGV Closed and TGV Open tables by actual TGV position. This is the TGVs-closed side. Retune when changing intake, cams or head flow.

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Open)
table.description: Volumetric efficiency by rpm and manifold pressure; feeds the ECU's air-mass model that defines engine load. The ECU blends the TGV Closed and TGV Open tables by actual TGV position. This is the TGVs-open side. Retune when changing intake, cams or head flow.

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency (fallback, all 1.0)
table.description: Fallback volumetric efficiency map used when the TGV-blended maps are not selected; flat 1.0.

table.name: Manifold Model Start Correction RPM Threshold
table.description: After start, once rpm passes this value (by coolant at start), the manifold model is pulled onto the MAF reading with the start gain (Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain) until model and MAF agree. Below this rpm the gain is 1.0. Normally leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain
table.description: Gain, by coolant at start, on how fast the manifold model is probably pulled onto the MAF reading right after start. Normally leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Pressure Rate Span (RPM)
table.description: How many samples (10 ms each) the ECU spans, by rpm, when measuring how fast manifold pressure is changing; that rate triggers the manifold model's transient corrections. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Flow Function
table.description: Physics curve for airflow through the throttle versus the pressure ratio across it, used by the manifold model that is corrected toward the MAF. Leave alone: it is an exact physical constant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Flow Temperature Correction
table.description: Temperature correction for throttle airflow in the manifold model (the standard square-root-of-temperature law). Leave alone: it is exact physics. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Flow Filter Weight
table.description: Smoothing of the modelled throttle airflow by pressure ratio: when pressures either side of the throttle are nearly equal (small, noisy flow) it is smoothed more. Normally leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Area from Throttle Position (Airflow Model)
table.description: Converts throttle position into effective throttle area (mm^2) for the airflow model and the throttle-based MAP substitute; about 2,150 mm^2 wide open. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)
table.description: Airflow per revolution versus throttle area per rpm. Used for a throttle-based MAP substitute (probably when the MAP sensor is faulted) and as an input to transient (tip-in) fueling. Change only for a different throttle body. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Gain Multiplier
table.description: Gain multiplier of the manifold-pressure model during (and one pass after) a rising pressure transient, in gear. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the rising-transient detection, in gear. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Hysteresis (Neutral)
table.description: Hysteresis on Manifold Model Rising Transient Threshold (Neutral) once the rising condition is met. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Threshold
table.description: How fast manifold pressure must rise (in gear) to count as a rising transient, which speeds up the ECU's manifold pressure model. Normally leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Threshold (Neutral)
table.description: Version of Manifold Model Rising Transient Threshold used with the transmission in neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the falling-transient detection, in gear. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient hysteresis, in neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold
table.description: A falling transient starts when manifold pressure drops this far below its filtered value (negative), in gear. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient threshold, in neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Engine Displacement
table.description: Engine displacement used by the airflow model.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
table.description: Modelled water in the exhaust at start, by coolant and intake temperature. If it is above the threshold, full A/F sensor heating waits until the model has dried out. Raise to delay A/F sensor heating on cold starts, lower to allow it earlier. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (Map)
table.description: Later-software version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Normally leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
table.description: Scales how fast water is modelled to condense in the exhaust, by exhaust flow (probably 1.0 = normal); more condensation keeps the front A/F sensor in its protected heating state longer. Normally leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
table.description: Correction of the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model for ignition timing (later timing = hotter exhaust). Does not affect fuel or timing. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
table.description: How quickly the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model follows its target, by coolant. Does not affect fuel or timing. Normally leave alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor
table.description: Correction of the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model for knock-related retard. Does not affect fuel or timing. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used instead of the other Map A tables while the car is at a standstill under high load (speed 5 km/h or less, pedal 80 % or more, load 40 % or more, for 1 s). Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature model map A by engine speed and load (Enriched set: Enriched is used while open-loop enrichment is active, No Enrichment otherwise). Raw model units, as on FA24, where this estimate decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling starts; on this ECU its consumer is not traced yet. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while an unidentified speed/pedal/load flag is set. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature model map B by engine speed and load (No Enrichment set: Enriched is used while open-loop enrichment is active, No Enrichment otherwise). Raw model units, as on FA24, where this estimate decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling starts; on this ECU its consumer is not traced yet. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Multiplier (1.0 = none) on the matching exhaust temperature map, by the timing deficit (how far fired timing sits from primary ignition), so retarded timing raises the modelled exhaust temperature. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Multiplier (1.0 = none) on the matching exhaust temperature map, by the timing deficit (how far fired timing sits from primary ignition), so retarded timing raises the modelled exhaust temperature. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Rising)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (A (Rising)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Rising, Standstill High Load)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (A (Rising, Standstill High Load)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Falling)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (A (Falling)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Falling, Standstill High Load)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (A (Falling, Standstill High Load)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Rising)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (B (Rising)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Rising, Standstill High Load)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (B (Rising, Standstill High Load)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Falling)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (B (Falling)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Falling, Standstill High Load)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate (B (Falling, Standstill High Load)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Step
table.description: Fuel-cut term of the exhaust temperature model: Step is added when the cylinder-cut count changes; Decay is the per-pass multiplier (1.0 = no decay) afterwards. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Decay
table.description: Fuel-cut term of the exhaust temperature model: Step is added when the cylinder-cut count changes; Decay is the per-pass multiplier (1.0 = no decay) afterwards. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (No Enrichment)
table.description: Second exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate (inferred), by rpm and load, with no enrichment active. When it gets high enough the ECU skips the delay before open loop fueling. Raising it brings open loop in sooner. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Enriched)
table.description: Second exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate (inferred), by rpm and load, while open loop enrichment is active. When it gets high enough the ECU skips the delay before open loop fueling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Version of Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map used while an unidentified flag (based on vehicle speed, pedal and load) is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Filter (Rising)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate ((Rising)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Filter (Rising, Standstill High Load)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate ((Rising, Standstill High Load)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Filter (Falling)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate ((Falling)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Filter (Falling, Standstill High Load)
table.description: Filter weight of the exhaust temperature estimate ((Falling, Standstill High Load)), by engine speed and load (or air flow for filter B). Raw units: the weight scale on this ECU is not confirmed. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Second Filter
table.description: Filter weight that smooths the second exhaust temperature estimate, by engine speed and load (raw). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Cam Target (TGV Open)
table.description: Intake cam target by engine speed and load with the TGVs Open (crank degrees). Blended with the other TGV state by TGV opening. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Cam Target (TGV Open, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam target used at altitude with the TGVs Open, blended in by barometric pressure (Cam Target Barometric Blend). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Cam Target (TGV Open, High Pedal)
table.description: Intake cam target with the TGVs open while a high-pedal flag is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Cam Target (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Altitude version of Intake Cam Target (TGV Open, High Pedal). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Intake Cam Target (TGV Closed)
table.description: Intake cam target by engine speed and load with the TGVs Closed (crank degrees). Blended with the other TGV state by TGV opening. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Cam Target (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam target used at altitude with the TGVs Closed, blended in by barometric pressure (Cam Target Barometric Blend). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by coolant temperature on Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset A (Altitude) and B (Sea Level), so those cold-engine exhaust cam corrections (applied in every TGV state) fade in or out with temperature. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target (TGV Open)
table.description: Exhaust cam target (degrees of retard from rest) by engine speed and load with the TGVs Open. The ECU blends the TGV-open and TGV-closed targets by TGV opening, adds the coolant offset, and blends each with its Altitude version by Cam Target Barometric Blend. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target (TGV Open, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam target, TGVs open, Altitude version: High Pedal replaces the normal TGV-open target while the high-pedal flag is set; Altitude versions are blended in by Cam Target Barometric Blend. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target (TGV Open, High Pedal)
table.description: Exhaust cam target, TGVs open, High Pedal version: High Pedal replaces the normal TGV-open target while the high-pedal flag is set; Altitude versions are blended in by Cam Target Barometric Blend. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam target, TGVs open, High Pedal, Altitude version: High Pedal replaces the normal TGV-open target while the high-pedal flag is set; Altitude versions are blended in by Cam Target Barometric Blend. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target (TGV Closed)
table.description: Exhaust cam target (degrees of retard from rest) by engine speed and load with the TGVs Closed. The ECU blends the TGV-open and TGV-closed targets by TGV opening, adds the coolant offset, and blends each with its Altitude version by Cam Target Barometric Blend. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Altitude version of Exhaust Cam Target (TGV Closed), blended in by Cam Target Barometric Blend. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset
table.description: Offset added to the exhaust cam target, scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset (Altitude)
table.description: Offset added to the exhaust cam target, scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Minimum (Torque, TGV Closed)
table.description: Lower limit on the exhaust cam target by engine speed and target torque (TGV Closed side, blended by TGV opening). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Minimum (Torque, TGV Open)
table.description: Lower limit on the exhaust cam target by engine speed and target torque (TGV Open side, blended by TGV opening). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling A
table.description: Upper limit on the exhaust cam target, interpolated by a temperature byte against three calibrations. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling B
table.description: Upper limit on the exhaust cam target, interpolated by a temperature byte against three calibrations. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling C
table.description: Upper limit on the exhaust cam target, interpolated by a temperature byte against three calibrations. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target B (TGV Closed)
table.description: A second exhaust target, TGV-blended, written to its own output; where the ECU uses it is not traced yet. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target B (TGV Open)
table.description: A second exhaust target, TGV-blended, written to its own output; where the ECU uses it is not traced yet. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Charge Air Temperature Offset
table.description: Exhaust cam offset by engine speed and charge air temperature, plus a coolant term, rate-limited into its own output while the AVCS is in one particular mode. Where the ECU adds this output is not traced yet. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Charge Air Temperature Offset (Alternate)
table.description: Part of the exhaust cam charge-air-temperature offset (alternate set or coolant term). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cam Target Barometric Blend
table.description: How much of the altitude cam targets is blended in, by barometric pressure (0 = normal targets, 1 = altitude targets). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
table.description: Base intake cam 1 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path. Confidence: inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 2, Legacy Path)
table.description: Base intake cam 2 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path. Confidence: inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
table.description: Base exhaust cam 1 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path. Confidence: inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust OCV Base Duty (Cam 2, Legacy Path)
table.description: Base exhaust cam 2 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path. Confidence: inferred. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description: Minimum engine speed for intake cam control by oil temperature. Below it the cams are held at rest and ignition fades to the AVCS Inactive timing tables. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving (pedal applied or moving). Larger values move the cam faster but can overshoot. Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) (Byte Output).

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing, added to the proportional term during active cam control. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving (pedal applied or moving). Larger values move the cam faster but can overshoot. Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) (Byte Output).

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Current Integral Step (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Integral step for the intake oil control valve current loop. a calibration setting forces the integral term to zero. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Multiplier on both intake oil control valve outputs by battery voltage, so the valves get the same effective drive as voltage changes. Always used. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Expected Current (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Expected intake oil control valve current for a given duty; the ECU compares the measured current with it to learn a correction factor. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description: Minimum engine speed for exhaust cam control by oil temperature; works like Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used at idle with the pedal fully released; otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. Larger values correct cam error faster. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving. Larger values move the cam towards its target faster but can overshoot. The idle variant is used with the pedal released at standstill. Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) (Byte Output).

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used at idle with the pedal fully released; otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving. Larger values move the cam towards its target faster but can overshoot. The idle variant is used with the pedal released at standstill. Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) (Byte Output).

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Current Integral Step (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Integral step for the exhaust oil control valve current loop. a calibration setting forces the exhaust integral term to zero. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Multiplier on both exhaust oil control valve outputs by battery voltage, so the valves get the same effective drive as voltage changes. Always used. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Expected Current (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Expected exhaust oil control valve current for a given duty; the ECU compares measured current against it to learn a correction. Same role as Intake AVCS OCV Expected Current. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start
table.description: Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Positive Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving intake cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both intake cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Positive Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle intake cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both intake cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Negative Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle intake cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both intake cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Negative Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving intake cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both intake cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp, Settled) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the intake oil control valve duty for normal running once cam control has been active a while. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the intake oil control valve duty, used only for the first moments of cam control after power-up; afterwards the Settled table is used. Probably compensates the valve coil warming with the oil. Edit together with the Settled table. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 1)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the intake cam 1 oil control valve current correction (limited to 0.5-1.5). Larger steps learn faster but can hunt. Used while valve duty is at least 20 %. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 2)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the intake cam 2 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the cam 1 table. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp, Settled) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the exhaust oil control valve duty, used for normal running once cam control has been active. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the exhaust oil control valve duty, used only briefly before the first active cam-control pass; afterwards the Settled table is used. Edit together with the Settled table. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 1)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the intake tables. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 2)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the intake tables. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the intake cam damping term for both cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Positive Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both exhaust cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Positive Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both exhaust cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Negative Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both exhaust cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Negative Error) (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both exhaust cams. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing, added to the proportional term during active cam control. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing; added to the proportional term during active cam control. More damping reduces overshoot. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing; added to the proportional term during active cam control. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor (Cams 1 and 2)
table.description: Multiplier on the exhaust cam rate-feedback term by oil temperature, cam 1 controller. Identified from this ECU's code. Cam 1 and cam 2 read this same table.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Speed Minimum (Baro, Oil Temp)
table.description: Floor on the idle speed target by barometric pressure and oil temperature; the ECU idles at no less than this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request (Alternate)
table.description: Minimum idle speed requested by another module over CAN, by request code. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Alternate B)
table.description: Alternative remap of the CAN idle speed request, used when an unidentified CAN flag is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Alternate)
table.description: Remaps the CAN idle speed request before it is applied. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Post-Start Mode Exit Coolant
table.description: Coolant temperature, by coolant at start, at which idle leaves the post-start mode for normal warm idle (it also leaves once the car moves). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, RPM Error)
table.description: Correction to Idle Air Reduction In Drive by rpm error (actual minus target) and coolant, for automatic/CVT cars idling in Drive. Never used on a manual car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, Coolant)
table.description: Idle air taken away, by coolant, while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive (pedal released, slow) to offset the load of the transmission. Never used on a manual car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/C Idle Air (Alternate, Target RPM)
table.description: A/C idle air by an unidentified CAN load value and idle target rpm, for an alternate A/C idle-air path. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Kick Duration (Alternate)
table.description: How long the alternate A/C idle air kick is held, by an unidentified CAN code. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward (AT/CVT, State 0/5)
