table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward, used in two transmission states only: extra or less idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Electrical Load Idle Air Hold Release (Alternator Command)
table.description: Flag table by alternator command that decides when the CAN load-value idle air adder (Idle Air Adder, CAN Load Value table) may increase while battery voltage is low. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Adder (CAN Load Value)
table.description: Extra idle air by a load value received over CAN, probably electrical load (not confirmed), added to the accessory idle air. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air from Throttle Area (Torque Request)
table.description: Converts a throttle area back into idle air units when another module requests torque over CAN. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Decay (Neutral)
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms after End Time, by start type and coolant (smaller = faster fade). Part of a timed post-start air bump. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Decay (In Gear)
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms after End Time, by start type and coolant (smaller = faster fade). Part of a timed post-start air bump. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay
table.description: Time after start, by start type and coolant at start, before the post-start idle air starts to decay (rpm must also have reached the idle target). Longer = extra air held longer. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air IAT Add
table.description: Added to Post-Start Staged Air Level by intake air temperature, for the timed post-start air bump. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Low Voltage Idle Request Threshold (Alternator Command)
table.description: Battery voltage threshold, by alternator command, for a low-voltage idle-up request. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart, TGV Closed)
table.description: Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart with the TGVs closed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description: Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart, by start type and coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay (TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air Decay: multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air after the decay delay. Smaller = faster fade. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air once rpm has reached the idle target and Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay has passed, by start type and coolant. Smaller = faster fade. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Minimum Idle Air (Moving in Gear)
table.description: Floor on idle air by rpm (and coolant) whenever the car is moving in gear, so the throttle cannot close below it; acts mainly as a dashpot when the pedal is released (inferred). Raise to soften throttle closing on decel; lower for faster rpm drop. Not used at standstill or in neutral. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Minimum Idle Air (Moving in Gear) (Mode 1)
table.description: Floor on idle air by rpm (and coolant) whenever the car is moving in gear, so the throttle cannot close below it; acts mainly as a dashpot when the pedal is released (inferred). Raise to soften throttle closing on decel; lower for faster rpm drop. Not used at standstill or in neutral. Mode 1: the idle routine picks one of three copies by a mode value (0, 1 or 2) it sets each pass from four status flags; the flags' meaning is not identified. Minimum Idle Air (Moving in Gear) is mode 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level (Neutral)
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level (In Gear)
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial, TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air (Initial): extra idle air right after start by start type and coolant, held and then decayed once rpm reaches the idle target. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial)
table.description: Extra idle air right after start, by start type (first start, restart, after a stall, remote start; start-type meanings inferred) and coolant. It is held after start, then decays by Post-Start Idle Air Decay once rpm reaches the idle target. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Key-On/Cranking)
table.description: Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure, used at key-on and while cranking. The two Running copies hold the same data: edit all three together. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Running, A/C Off)
table.description: Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure while running with the A/C off. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Running, A/C On)
table.description: Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure while running with the A/C on. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Positive)
table.description: How fast the idle feedback air kept when leaving idle is bled off, by rpm change rate; this acts like a dashpot (inferred). Larger = faster release. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Negative)
table.description: How fast a negative leftover of idle feedback air is released after leaving idle, by rpm change rate. Larger = cancels sooner. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Negative)
table.description: Limit on a negative idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Positive)
table.description: Limit on a positive idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (A/C Off)
table.description: How fast the long-term idle air learning follows the current correction with the A/C off, by time since the last learning transfer. Larger = learns faster but less stable. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (Before First Transfer)
table.description: Long-term idle learning speed used after an idle-learn reset until the first learned value has been stored. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Learn Bias
table.description: Offset added to the long-term idle air learning by a drive-history index: long idling pushes the learned idle air down, sustained driving pushes it up (purpose, e.g. heat soak, inferred). Index movement is set by Idle Learn Bias Index Step. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Learn Bias Index Step
table.description: How the drive-history index for Idle Learn Bias moves every 2 s, by vehicle speed (only with coolant at or above 80 degC). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (A/C On)
table.description: How fast the long-term idle air learning follows the current correction with the A/C on, by time since the last learning transfer. Larger = learns faster but less stable. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle State Speed Error Threshold (Lower)
table.description: Idle controller state selection, by coolant and engine speed: while stopped, engine speed minus a received idle-speed request must be at or above this for state group 1; below it, group 2. Only used while that request is valid (received over CAN, probably from a transmission controller; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle State Speed Error Threshold (Upper)
table.description: Idle controller state selection, by coolant and engine speed: in neutral, engine speed must be more than this above the received idle-speed request (and past Idle State Minimum Time Since Start) for the high-idle state (group 1). Only used while that request is valid. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle State Settle Time
table.description: Idle controller state selection, by coolant and engine speed: how long the stopped car must meet Idle State Speed Error Threshold (Lower) before the settled-idle state is entered. Unit: controller passes (rate not read). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle Speed Torque Feedback Reference Torque
table.description: Reference torque by rpm that scales the idle torque feedback (P and D): a larger value gives a smaller correction. Must not be set to 0 ft-lb, which zeroes the feedback. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle State Stopped Speed Threshold
table.description: Vehicle speed below which the idle controller treats the car as stopped. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle State Minimum Time Since Start
table.description: Time since start the engine must pass before the idle controller's high-idle state can be entered. Counter units (rate not read). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle State Speed Error Hysteresis (Lower)
table.description: Hysteresis on Idle State Speed Error Threshold (Lower). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Idle State Speed Error Hysteresis (Upper)
table.description: Hysteresis on Idle State Speed Error Threshold (Upper). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open)
table.description: Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Reduction Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by rpm and load that reduces the target EGR rate while an unidentified module requests it and EGR flow is present. When the request is active is not known. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by barometric pressure on EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by coolant on the target EGR rate. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Enable Minimum Air after Start
table.description: Amount of air (probably the air drawn since start), by coolant at start, that must pass before EGR is enabled. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate DAM Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the target EGR rate by the knock learning value (probably DAM). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder
table.description: Term added to EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate after multiplying by EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder Multiplier (barometric pressure), by engine speed and load. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Closed)
table.description: Main EGR rate target (% of intake charge, probably external EGR) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed. 0 = no EGR. Raising it adds more exhaust gas at light load. Capped by EGR Target Rate Maximum. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Open)
table.description: Main EGR rate target (% of intake charge, probably external EGR) by rpm and load while the TGVs are open. 0 = no EGR. Capped by EGR Target Rate Maximum. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Alternate, TGV Closed)
table.description: Alternate EGR rate target by rpm and throttle position (instead of load) with the TGVs closed. The alternate pair is chosen by a calibration switch. Its input here is the electronic throttle's opening, 0-100 % quartered to 0.4 % per count (inferred from the code). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Alternate, TGV Open)
table.description: Alternate EGR rate target by rpm and throttle position (instead of load) with the TGVs open. The alternate pair is chosen by a calibration switch. Its input here is the electronic throttle's opening, 0-100 % quartered to 0.4 % per count (inferred from the code). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Closed)
table.description: Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs closed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Valve Flow Model
table.description: Estimated EGR flow by pressure difference across the valve and valve position. Used both for the actual EGR flow estimate and for the flow feedback, so edits change both. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Valve Position from Target Flow
table.description: Feed-forward EGR valve position (steps) for a target EGR flow; feedback is added on top. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Valve Flow Feedback Integral Step
table.description: How fast the EGR valve feedback corrects position, by the error between target and modelled flow. Positive opens the valve. Larger = faster correction, more risk of hunting. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Enable RPM Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when rpm is at or below this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Enable Intake Air Temp Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when intake air temperature is at or above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Enable Battery Voltage Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when battery voltage is at or above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Enable Coolant Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when coolant is at or below this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Enable Load Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when load is at or above this. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Valve Feedback Integral Minimum
table.description: Lower limit of the EGR valve flow-feedback correction (how far feedback may close the valve below feed-forward). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Maximum
table.description: Hard cap on the target EGR rate. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Open Fraction from Position (one direction)
table.description: Converts TGV position into the TGV open fraction used to blend TGV-open and TGV-closed maps (one direction of travel). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Open Fraction from Position (other direction)
table.description: Converts TGV position into the TGV open fraction used to blend TGV-open and TGV-closed maps (other direction of travel). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Drive Duty (Closing)
table.description: Motor duty used to drive the TGVs towards their closed stop, by valve position (closed meaning inferred). Leave alone unless the TGV actuators are changed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Drive Duty (Opening)
table.description: Motor duty used to drive the TGVs towards their open stop, by valve position (open meaning inferred). Leave alone unless the TGV actuators are changed. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Motor Duty Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the TGV motor drive duty by coolant and battery voltage, so the valves move reliably when cold or at low voltage. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Close Delay
table.description: How long the TGV-close conditions must hold before the TGVs actually close, by vehicle speed. Longer = fewer TGV switches during brief light-load moments. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment (Opening)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to open, by rpm and load; faded by its hold time and decay step. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment (Opening, Alternate)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to open, by rpm and load, Alternate; faded by its hold time and decay step. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Mode 2, TGV Closed)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Mode 2, TGV Open)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Mode 3, TGV Closed)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Mode 3, TGV Open)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (Mode 2, TGV Closed)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (Mode 2, TGV Open)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (Mode 3, TGV Closed)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (Mode 3, TGV Open)
table.description: Mode 2 / Mode 3: used instead of the main table while the mode value the EGR target routine reads is 2 or 3 (probably combustion mode 2 / 3, catalyst heating; inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close (Drive Mode 1, Default). They reopen once torque rises above the matching Exit table. Coolant, air quantity and IAT conditions also apply. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, above which a TGV close request clears (Drive Mode 1, Default). Keep it above the matching Enter table. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close (Drive Mode 2, Sport). They reopen once torque rises above the matching Exit table. Coolant, air quantity and IAT conditions also apply. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, above which a TGV close request clears (Drive Mode 2, Sport). Keep it above the matching Enter table. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Other Drive Modes)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close (Other Drive Modes). They reopen once torque rises above the matching Exit table. Coolant, air quantity and IAT conditions also apply. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Other Drive Modes)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, above which a TGV close request clears (Other Drive Modes). Keep it above the matching Enter table. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Start Mode)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close (Start Mode). They reopen once torque rises above the matching Exit table. Coolant, air quantity and IAT conditions also apply. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Start Mode)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, above which a TGV close request clears (Start Mode). Keep it above the matching Enter table. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Offset
table.description: Torque offset added to every TGV torque threshold except the start-mode pair, by rpm and an unidentified input. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV IAT Threshold
table.description: Intake air temperature, by vehicle speed, below which a TGV close request is held off. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum
table.description: Minimum coolant temperature for the TGVs to close. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum Hysteresis
table.description: Taken off TGV Coolant Minimum once the coolant condition holds. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter)
table.description: Air quantity below which the TGVs may close (raw units, quantity not identified yet). Raise it with the Exit value to let the TGVs close at higher air flow. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Exit)
table.description: Air quantity above which a TGV close request clears (raw units). Keep it at or above the Enter value. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV IAT Threshold Hysteresis
table.description: Added to TGV IAT Threshold once intake air is below it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Start Mode Select
table.description: Combustion mode in which the start-mode torque thresholds are used (0 = cranking). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: TGV Hold Combustion Mode
table.description: Combustion mode in which TGV closing is held off (0 = cranking). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Cancel Speed
table.description: Speed below which cruise control cancels (and the set speed is cleared), by meter (market) code. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed Filter Weight
table.description: Smoothing weight for the vehicle speed used by cruise control, by speed error and speed. Larger = less smoothing, quicker reaction. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. This is the standard km/h version. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. Standard mph version. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed from CAN Speed
table.description: Converts the CAN vehicle speed into the speed used by cruise control, per meter (market) code, as a straight line (scale and offset). The offsets probably make the set speed match the speedometer. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter code (km/h Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter code (mph Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. km/h version with the meter cruise option. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. mph-meter version with the meter cruise option. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Cruise Excess Acceleration Threshold (Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: With one cruise option and an alternate flag only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 0.2 s while cruise is on without pedal input, cruise ends (probably a runaway check). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x23)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after a short tap of the raise (accelerate) switch (tap meaning inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Default)
table.description: Main cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error, used while holding speed and in all states without their own table. Higher = more aggressive throttle response. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0xB0)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after a short tap of the lowering (coast) switch (tap meaning inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Catch-Up)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error, used while the car catches up to a set speed changed by holding a switch (inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0xC0)
table.description: Cruise controller gain used in a cruise state probably linked to the lowering switch (inferred), when Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach) is not active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x40)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after the raise switch, while not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed. Higher = more aggressive throttle response. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error while approaching a new set speed, until within about 3 km/h of it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Ramp-Down Rate
table.description: How fast, by vehicle speed, brake override ramps the accelerator signal down. Larger = faster torque cut when brake and accelerator overlap. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Floor
table.description: Lowest pedal value, by vehicle speed, that brake override ramps the accelerator signal down to. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Rate (Pedal Held)
table.description: How fast, by vehicle speed, the pedal limit is raised again after the brake is released while the driver keeps the accelerator pressed. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Maximum
table.description: Upper limit, by barometric pressure, of a modelled brake-booster vacuum. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Time
table.description: Time, by vehicle speed, over which full pedal is restored after brake override ends (recovery ends early if the pedal is released or reached). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Override Delay
table.description: How long the brake must be pressed over a held accelerator, by pedal position and speed, before brake override starts cutting the pedal signal (above 7 km/h). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Manifold Threshold
table.description: Manifold-vacuum threshold, by barometric pressure, for a brake-booster vacuum model. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Brake Override Deceleration Threshold (No Pressure Signal)

scaling.units: ms per mph of speed drop

scaling.category: ms per km/h of speed drop
scaling.units: ms per km/h of speed drop

table.description: Deceleration needed (by pedal and speed) to confirm braking when the brake-pressure signal is not available, so brake override can still act from the brake switch. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: VDC Torque Request Correction
table.description: Correction, by the gap between the stability control (VDC) torque request and actual engine torque, that sets how tightly the ECU limits target torque during a VDC torque reduction (VDC meaning inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Charging Feedback Proportional
table.description: Charging voltage feedback proportional term by voltage error. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Alternator Command from Target Voltage
table.description: Alternator command by target charging voltage. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Charge Control Delay After Start (SOC, Battery Sensor)
table.description: Charging control: Delay After Start (SOC, Battery Sensor). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Charge Control Charge After Start (SOC)
table.description: Charging control: Charge After Start (SOC). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (A/C, CAN Value)
table.description: Radiator fan duty with the A/C requested, by an unidentified CAN value. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant)
table.description: Radiator fan duty by coolant used while a CAN-received value is high (above its latch threshold), and as the fallback; below the threshold the CAN Value Low tables are used. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, CAN Value Low)
table.description: Radiator fan duty by coolant, used while a CAN-received value is low (below its latch threshold) and no override flag is set. Above the threshold Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant) is used instead. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, CAN Value Low, Alternate)
table.description: Used instead of Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, CAN Value Low) when a second, unidentified flag is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, Alternate Flag)
table.description: Radiator fan duty by coolant that replaces the other coolant duty tables while an unidentified flag is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Battery Charged SOC Threshold
table.description: Above this state of charge, early in each charge cycle, the ECU decides the battery is charged and switches to the Battery Charged target voltage. Raising it makes the charge cut happen less often. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Battery Charged SOC Hysteresis
table.description: Once the battery counts as charged, the state of charge must rise this much above the threshold to stay so. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Battery Charged Check Window
table.description: How long into each charge cycle the battery-charged check is made. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Charge Limit
table.description: Adaptive charging also ends once this much charge has gone back into the battery (raw units). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Time Limit
table.description: Adaptive charging (the self-computed target) ends after this time in the cycle. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Charge Cycle Length
table.description: Length of one charge-control cycle; the battery-charged decision is made again at the start of each. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Battery State of Charge Reset Value
table.description: The state of charge the ECU assumes when its estimate is reset. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow Boost Limit Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description: Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by the ratio of the current boost limit to Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque). Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow IAT Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description: Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by intake temperature ratio. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate
table.description: How fast, by rpm, the engine torque reported over CAN to other modules (for example stability control) fades out at a fuel cut and returns after it. It does not change fuelling or throttle. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate. The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate, or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Gear Detection Ratio Upper Limit (Gear 1)
table.description: The ECU works out the gear from engine speed divided by vehicle speed. It reports gear n while that ratio is below the upper limit and at or above the lower limit; the overlap between neighbouring gears is the hysteresis. The limits sit midway between the 6MT gear ratios, so change them only for a different gearbox, final drive or tyre size. The detected gear is the Gear axis of many torque, ignition and drive-mode tables. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.description: The ECU works out the gear from engine speed divided by vehicle speed. It reports gear n while that ratio is below the upper limit and at or above the lower limit; the overlap between neighbouring gears is the hysteresis. table.name: MAF Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts MAF sensor voltage to airflow (g/s) in 64 fixed steps from 0 to 4.92 V; this airflow drives the ECU's air model, load and fuel. Rescale every point when fitting a bigger intake or a different MAF, and keep peak flow below the P0103 voltage limit. An internal 218 g/s cap on one copy of the airflow affects only purge, TGV, monitors and similar side functions, not fuel, load or timing. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: MAF Correction (Temperature)
table.description: MAF reading correction by an intake temperature. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling
table.description: Front A/F sensor scaling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description: How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: MAP Sensor Multiplier
table.description: Gain of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. For a 3-bar or larger sensor set it to the new sensor's slope and set MAP Sensor Offset to match. The ECU's MAP value cannot go above 256 kPa absolute (about 22 psi boost at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted, so anything higher reads as 256 kPa. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: MAP Sensor Offset
table.description: Offset of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, i.e. the sensor's reading extrapolated to 0 V. Set it together with MAP Sensor Multiplier when fitting a different MAP sensor. The result is still limited to 256 kPa absolute. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0192)
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage below which P0192 (circuit low) is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0193)
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage above which P0193 (circuit high) is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0112)
table.description: Voltage below which the main IAT sensor is flagged as shorted (reads impossibly hot, P0112). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage Low Limit (P0097)
table.description: Voltage below which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0097). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage High Limit (P0098)
table.description: Voltage above which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0098). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0197)
table.description: Voltage below which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0197). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0118)
table.description: Voltage above which the coolant sensor is flagged as open (P0118). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0198)
table.description: Voltage above which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0198). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Stopped Flag Clear Speed
table.description: Speed band of a vehicle-stopped flag: the flag is set below the Set speed and cleared at or above the Clear speed; between the two it holds its state unless a timer runs out. The flag is sent on to the communication layer; what uses it there is not read. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Vehicle Stopped Flag Set Speed
table.description: Speed band of a vehicle-stopped flag: the flag is set below the Set speed and cleared at or above the Clear speed; between the two it holds its state unless a timer runs out. The flag is sent on to the communication layer; what uses it there is not read. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Enable
table.description: Calibration switch byte. Matched to the FA24 switch of this name by value and code context; check the bit meanings before changing it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling: Use Alternate Map
table.description: Calibration switch byte. Matched to the FA24 switch of this name by value and code context; check the bit meanings before changing it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Enable
table.description: Calibration switch byte. Matched to the FA24 switch of this name by value and code context; check the bit meanings before changing it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: VE: Use AVCS-Not-Ready Table
table.description: Calibration switch byte. Matched to the FA24 switch of this name by value and code context; check the bit meanings before changing it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT
table.description: Calibration switch byte. Matched to the FA24 switch of this name by value and code context; check the bit meanings before changing it. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 1)
Fuel rail pressure plus rpm/load offset

table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 1. Set 1 is looked up by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset; set 2 by rail pressure alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)
table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 2. Set 2 is looked up by rail pressure alone; set 1 by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
table.description: Rail pressure target used in normal running mode only during a start delay before the engine counts as running. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target used instead of Target Rail Pressure while the accelerator is fully released (cranking or running), by coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the injector pulse (1.0 = none) by pulse width and rail pressure, for the injector's non-linear short-pulse region. It is applied after Injector Flow Compensation and before Injector Latency is added. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no such table. If you change injectors, revisit this together with Injector Latency and Injector Scaling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)
table.description: Fixed rail pressure target during stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating), used while a separate state flag is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Requested torque by accelerator pedal and engine speed for the default drive mode. On the manual car the ECU uses it only while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is off; while the switch is on, the per-gear maps (Neutral, Gear 1-6) of this mode are used instead. On an AT/CVT car it is blended with the AT/CVT map. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

Like the default mode, this per-gear set replaces the mode's base map on the manual car while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is on. The manual car probably stays in drive mode 1 (inferred). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, Neutral) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 1)
Fuel rail pressure plus rpm/load offset

table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 1. Set 1 is looked up by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset; set 2 by rail pressure alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)
table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 2. Set 2 is looked up by rail pressure alone; set 1 by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
table.description: Rail pressure target used in normal running mode only during a start delay before the engine counts as running. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target used instead of Target Rail Pressure while the accelerator is fully released (cranking or running), by coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the injector pulse (1.0 = none) by pulse width and rail pressure, for the injector's non-linear short-pulse region. It is applied after Injector Flow Compensation and before Injector Latency is added. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no such table. If you change injectors, revisit this together with Injector Latency and Injector Scaling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)

The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT Index 1), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Idle State Group 1, Alt)
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Idle State Group 2, Alt)
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature model map B by engine speed and load (Enriched set: Enriched is used while open-loop enrichment is active, No Enrichment otherwise). Raw model units, as on FA24, where this estimate decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling starts; on this ECU its consumer is not traced yet. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Retard Multiplier (No Enrichment)
table.description: Multiplier (1.0 = none) on the matching exhaust temperature map, by the timing deficit (how far fired timing sits from primary ignition), so retarded timing raises the modelled exhaust temperature. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start
table.description: How long after every start the cams are held at their rest position before cam control begins, by coolant temperature at start. Raise for a longer hold, lower to start cam control sooner. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start (Second)
table.description: Delay after start before cam control begins, by coolant at start. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate
table.description: Estimated pressure upstream of the EGR valve (probably exhaust side) by rpm and load. The difference to manifold pressure sets the modelled EGR flow and decides whether EGR may be enabled. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 1)
Fuel rail pressure plus rpm/load offset

table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 1. Set 1 is looked up by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset; set 2 by rail pressure alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)
table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 2. Set 2 is looked up by rail pressure alone; set 1 by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
table.description: Rail pressure target used in normal running mode only during a start delay before the engine counts as running. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target used instead of Target Rail Pressure while the accelerator is fully released (cranking or running), by coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the injector pulse (1.0 = none) by pulse width and rail pressure, for the injector's non-linear short-pulse region. It is applied after Injector Flow Compensation and before Injector Latency is added. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no such table. If you change injectors, revisit this together with Injector Latency and Injector Scaling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)
table.description: Fixed rail pressure target during stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating), used while a separate state flag is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Decay Change (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Phase time of the tip-in lash retard (Drive Mode 1, Default), in passes counted from the tip-in: Decay Change. Before Start the retard is zero. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Attack Rate (Drive Mode 1, Default)
Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Decay Rate 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Decay Rate 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
Tip-In Lash Timing Retard Release Decay Rate (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Tip-in lash retard ramp, Drive Mode 1, Default: Release Decay Rate per pass. Attack Rate applies between the Start and Peak End times, Decay Rate 1 between Peak End and Decay Change, Decay Rate 2 after that, and Release Decay Rate once the tip-in condition ends. table.description: Requested torque by accelerator pedal and engine speed for the default drive mode. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 4) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). The ECU reads this table only on AT/CVT coding; this ROM is coded manual.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, Neutral)
table.description: Requested torque by accelerator pedal and engine speed for Neutral (the ECU's gear count: 1-6, with 0 taken as neutral, inferred) for the default drive mode. On the manual car, while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is on, this per-gear set is the pedal map: the ECU uses these instead of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default). Above gear 6 it holds the last value. The result is capped by Requested Torque Cap (Drive Mode 1, Default). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). Like the default mode, this per-gear set replaces the mode's base map on the manual car while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is on. The manual car probably stays in drive mode 1 (inferred). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, Gear 1) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 1) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 1). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT Index 2), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. The ECU reads this copy instead of Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (Gear 6, From 1800 RPM) while the drive mode (SI-Drive) is 2, Sport (position inferred from the FA20 platform, as for the requested torque maps). Edit this copy to change Sport only, or both this copy and Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (Gear 6, From 1800 RPM) to keep the modes alike.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1, Drive Mode 2 Sport)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 1: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). This calibration is coded AT/CVT, so this table is in use.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0.
