table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 1)
Fuel rail pressure plus rpm/load offset

table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 1. Set 1 is looked up by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset; set 2 by rail pressure alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)
table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 2. Set 2 is looked up by rail pressure alone; set 1 by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied), used while a separate state flag is set. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Alternate Set)

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the injector pulse (1.0 = none) by pulse width and rail pressure, for the injector's non-linear short-pulse region. It is applied after Injector Flow Compensation and before Injector Latency is added. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no such table. If you change injectors, revisit this together with Injector Latency and Injector Scaling. Identified from this ECU's code.

The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, Gear 6), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 1)
Fuel rail pressure plus rpm/load offset

table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 1. Set 1 is looked up by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset; set 2 by rail pressure alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)
table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 2. Set 2 is looked up by rail pressure alone; set 1 by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)

Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the injector pulse (1.0 = none) by pulse width and rail pressure, for the injector's non-linear short-pulse region. It is applied after Injector Flow Compensation and before Injector Latency is added. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no such table. If you change injectors, revisit this together with Injector Latency and Injector Scaling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Requested torque by accelerator pedal and engine speed for the default drive mode. On the manual car the ECU uses it only while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is off; while the switch is on, the per-gear maps (Neutral, Gear 1-6) of this mode are used instead. On an AT/CVT car it is blended with the AT/CVT map. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). This calibration is coded AT/CVT: the ECU blends this map with the AT/CVT one, so it is in use.

Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). This calibration is coded AT/CVT, so this table is in use.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, Neutral)

Above gear 6 it holds the last value. The result is capped by Requested Torque Cap (Drive Mode 1, Default). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, Neutral) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). The ECU reads this table only on manual coding; this ROM is coded AT/CVT.

Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)

Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Index 1) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced. This calibration is coded AT/CVT, so this table is in use.

The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Index 2), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 1)
Fuel rail pressure plus rpm/load offset

table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 1. Set 1 is looked up by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset; set 2 by rail pressure alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)
table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 2. Set 2 is looked up by rail pressure alone; set 1 by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
table.description: Rail pressure target used in normal running mode only during a start delay before the engine counts as running. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target used instead of Target Rail Pressure while the accelerator is fully released (cranking or running), by coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the injector pulse (1.0 = none) by pulse width and rail pressure, for the injector's non-linear short-pulse region. It is applied after Injector Flow Compensation and before Injector Latency is added. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no such table. If you change injectors, revisit this together with Injector Latency and Injector Scaling. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)
table.description: Fixed rail pressure target during stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating), used while a separate state flag is set. Identified from this ECU's code.

Like the default mode, this per-gear set replaces the mode's base map on the manual car while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is on. The manual car probably stays in drive mode 1 (inferred). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, Gear 6) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced. The ECU reads this table only on manual coding; this ROM is coded AT/CVT.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 1) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 1). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 1), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT Index 8), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map. Identified from this ECU's code. The ECU also reads this table as: Primary Ignition (Second Set, TGV Open, AVCS Inactive).

table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. table.name: Injector Latency

table.name: Injector Latency Adder

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation

Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Requested torque by accelerator pedal and engine speed for the default drive mode. On the manual car the ECU uses it only while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is off; while the switch is on, the per-gear maps (Neutral, Gear 1-6) of this mode are used instead. On an AT/CVT car it is blended with the AT/CVT map. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value).

Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT Index 1) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced. The ECU reads this table only on AT/CVT coding; this ROM is coded manual.

table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used for a while after a combustion-mode change while final timing is still well short of the spark target. Leave alone unless you know the model. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 1)
Fuel rail pressure plus rpm/load offset

table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 1. Set 1 is looked up by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset; set 2 by rail pressure alone. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)
table.description: Injector flow compensation by rail pressure, set 2. Set 2 is looked up by rail pressure alone; set 1 by rail pressure plus an rpm/load offset. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Alternate Set)
table.description: Alternate-set version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1), used while a separate state flag is set. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
table.description: Rail pressure target used in normal running mode only during a start delay before the engine counts as running. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target used instead of Target Rail Pressure while the accelerator is fully released (cranking or running), by coolant. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the injector pulse (1.0 = none) by pulse width and rail pressure, for the injector's non-linear short-pulse region. It is applied after Injector Flow Compensation and before Injector Latency is added. Identified from this ECU's code; the FA24 definitions have no such table. table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). This calibration is coded AT/CVT, so this table is in use.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT)
table.description: AT/CVT partner of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp): on a car coded AT/CVT the request is a blend of the two by a weight from the transmission side. Not used on the manual car. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). This calibration is coded AT/CVT, so this table is in use.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 7, AT/CVT), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. table.description: Requested torque by accelerator pedal and engine speed for the default drive mode. On the manual car the ECU uses it only while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is off; while the switch is on, the per-gear maps (Neutral, Gear 1-6) of this mode are used instead. On an AT/CVT car it is blended with the AT/CVT map. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). This calibration is coded AT/CVT: the ECU blends this map with the AT/CVT one, so it is in use.

The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 8), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

Like the default mode, this per-gear set replaces the mode's base map on the manual car while Requested Torque Gear Maps Switch is on. The manual car probably stays in drive mode 1 (inferred). Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Its (Monitor) copy, Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, Gear 2) (Monitor), must hold the same data unless Torque Monitor Fault Mode is 0 (see that value). Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced. The ECU reads this table only on manual coding; this ROM is coded AT/CVT.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 1) (Monitor)
table.description: Monitor-layer copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Index 1). The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). table.name: Target Rail Pressure

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (set 2)

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0, Alternate Set)

Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Start)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant that replaces the main map while a start condition is active. Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 1)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 1. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Idle State Group 2)
table.description: Target rail pressure by coolant in combustion mode 1, idle controller state group 2. Group 1: out of neutral, moving, or engine speed at or above a received idle-speed request; group 2: neutral (default state) or stopped below the request. On the manual car, probably without that request (inferred), group 1 = out of neutral and group 2 = neutral. Edit both together unless you know the difference. Combustion mode is the cold-start sequence: 0 cranking, 1 first warm-up phase, 2 stratified catalyst heating, 3 catalyst-heating phase 2, 4 normal running. Idle state groups: Group 1 is used out of neutral, while moving, or at or above a received idle-speed request; Group 2 in neutral (the default state) or stopped below that request. On this manual car probably in gear (Group 1) versus neutral (Group 2) (inferred). Identified from this ECU's code.

table.name: Injector Small Pulse Compensation

The ECU's torque monitor recomputes the torque the driver may have from these copies and checks the engine against it; if the check fails, the ECU closes the throttle and keeps it closed until the engine is restarted (inferred from the code). Nothing else reads it. Keep it identical to Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Index 6), or set Torque Monitor Fault Mode to 0. Drive mode is the SI-Drive request received over CAN: 1 Default (also used when no valid request arrives), 2 Sport, 3 Intelligent, 4 Sport Sharp (positions inferred from the FA20 platform). The ECU decodes the request from three bits: the two bits that give Sport and Sport Sharp on their own give mode 7 when both are set. What selects that combination on the car is not identified. Identified from this ECU's code. Axis input inferred: this axis shares its breakpoint array with a table whose input was traced.
